what: Somnigroup is the mattress company formed when Tempur Sealy bought Mattress Firm. It makes Tempur-Pedic, Sealy and Stearns & Foster beds and now also sells them through its own stores.
customers: Shoppers buying a mattress roughly once a decade, through its own stores, other retailers and online.
money: mattresses made and sold in the United States and Canada
its own store chain, acquired in 2025
Tempur and Sealy sales in Europe and Asia
moat: Owning both the brands people ask for and the stores where most mattresses are bought, which is a position no rival has.
risks: $6.7B of debt against $135M of cash, taken on to buy Mattress Firm
Mattress demand follows house moves, which are depressed by high mortgage rates
Regulators required store divestitures as a condition of the deal
opportunities: Analysts see about 44% upside, the widest gap in home furnishings
Revenue jumped from $4.9B to $7.5B as the retail chain came in
Selling its own brands in its own stores keeps the retail margin as well as the manufacturing one
watch: Same-store sales at Mattress Firm and progress paying down the acquisition debt.
